passage: Half past eleven at night, and the phone buzzed on the shelf among the rice sacks in the family shop near Kolhapur where Pranav worked from home while on call. Payments were failing. Every minute, someone at a counter is failing to pay, he thought. I don't need the reason yet. The release went out two hours ago; rolling it back takes five minutes, and I know how. Hunting the bug could take hours. He typed the rollback, watched the dashboard, and saw the failures thin out and stop. Then he wrote in the team channel, 'Rolled back the latest release, payments recovering, will look at the cause in daylight,' and asked Charu, who owned that release, to check the logs when she woke.

qa.a: Pranav rolled back the release that had gone out two hours earlier.

qa.q: What was Pranav worried about when he chose to act before finding the cause?
qa.a: Pranav was worried that every minute someone at a counter failed to pay, which pushed him to stop the damage first.

qa.q: What could Pranav do if the rollback had not fixed the payments?
qa.a: Pranav could ask a second person to investigate while he keeps watching the dashboard, so diagnosis carries on with shared work.

qa.q: How might Charu see the rollback of the release?
qa.a: Charu might feel a little disappointed, but also relieved that customers recovered and the cause can be checked calmly in daylight.

grounding: Shows an on-call engineer rolling back the latest release at once during a payments outage and leaving diagnosis for later.
